title: EFC v2.1 – Complete Edition
description: Presents the Complete Edition of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC v2.1), a unified thermodynamic framework where a continuous energy–entropy flow field Ef generates spacetime structure, cosmic dynamics, and reflexive cognition. The paper adds an Energy-Flow Ontology, explicit continuity and conservation laws, cognitive thermodynamics, an Intelligence–Matter Exchange (IMX) model, observational links with testable predictions, and a computational implementation plan.

energy_continuity.description: Explicit conservation of energy flow: changes in energy density are balanced by the divergence of the energy-flow field.

constitutive_Ef.description: Minimal constitutive relation coupling the energy-flow field to entropy, decreasing linearly with increasing entropy.

c_regulation.description: Emergent regulation of the effective local light speed by the thermodynamic state (energy density).

geometry_coupling.description: Gravitational field equations including additional stress-energy from entropy gradients and flow currents.

symmetry_principle.description: Bidirectional thermodynamic symmetry linking entropic expansion and informational (inward) evolution.

cem_definition.description: Cognitive thermodynamics: consciousness modeled as resonance in non-equilibrium gradients of Ef and entropy.

imx_definition.description: Defines Intelligence–Matter Exchange as the sensitivity of cognitive state to changes in energy flow.

imx_continuity.description: Continuity-like equation for IMX, balancing propagation and dissipation with coupling to energy-flow divergence and entropy production.

key_results.main_finding: EFC v2.1 consolidates a falsifiable, thermodynamic cosmology linking structure, dynamics, and cognition via a conserved energy–entropy flow field and provides concrete, dataset-specific predictions.

sealed_predictions.statement: CMB shows a ~0.05% excess in temperature anisotropy at multipole ℓ ≈ 2500 as a thermal residual of ΔS relative to ΛCDM baselines.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-ℓ CMB TT/TE/EE spectra from Planck/ACT (and ancillary analyses cited) showing no such excess after foreground/systematic controls.

sealed_predictions.statement: Local H0 measurements differ by ~5–7% from the global value due to spatial Ef gradients correlated with large-scale entropy environments.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Cross-correlation of environment metrics with distance-ladder H0 (SH0ES/TRGB) and DESI BAO+RSD analyses showing |ΔH0| < 1% with no environment dependence.

sealed_predictions.statement: Weak-lensing shear γ is reduced in high-entropy (high-S) regions (‘entropic halos’) relative to mass-only expectations.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic weak-lensing (SDSS, Euclid, LSST) finding no systematic γ suppression in high-S environments at <1% precision after baryonic corrections.

sealed_predictions.statement: Redshift-drift exhibits a nonlinear z(S) signature diverging from ΛCDM over decade-long baselines.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Direct redshift-drift measurements (ELT/Euclid programs) consistent with ΛCDM and excluding the EFC z(S) trend at ≥5σ.

sealed_predictions.statement: Gravitational-wave arrival times acquire path-dependent delays proportional to ∇S across void/halo transits.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-messenger timing (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA) and PTA (NANOGrav) showing no correlation between GW timing residuals and mapped entropy/flow gradients at predicted amplitudes.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-ℓ CMB analyses (Planck/ACT and successors) show no ~0.05% excess at ℓ ≈ 2500 after rigorous foreground/systematics treatment, decisively favoring ΛCDM at ≥5σ.
KC2: Environmental cross-checks find |ΔH0| < 1% with no statistically significant correlation between local H0 estimates and large-scale entropy/flow gradients.
KC3: Weak-lensing tomography detects no reduction of shear γ in high-S regions beyond baryonic effects, with shear–mass relations matching ΛCDM at <1% across environments.
KC4: Redshift-drift measurements over ≥10 years match ΛCDM and exclude the EFC-predicted nonlinear z(S) evolution at ≥5σ.
KC5: Gravitational-wave timing residuals show no correlation with mapped ∇S along lines of sight through voids/halos at the amplitudes required by EFC.
KC6: Implementations of EFC in CLASS/RAMSES/GADGET-4 fail to jointly fit CMB+BAO+SNe observables without extreme fine-tuning and are disfavored by AIC/BIC relative to ΛCDM.
